Paper node: Evading the strength–ductility trade-off dilemma in steel through gradient hierarchical nanotwins (2014). Cited 768 times before the cutoff; 2 papers in this graph say something specific about it.
Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can the strength of twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) steel be enhanced without sacrificing ductility, thereby evading the long-standing strength–ductility trade-off dilemma?. System: FeMnC TWIP steel (23.84% Mn, 0.61% C, balanced Fe) with a low stacking fault energy of 15–30 m Jm−2. Processing: Cylindrical samples were subjected to torsion (180° or 360°) at an angular loading rate of 0.05° s−1 to generate a gradient nanotwinned structure, followed by uniaxial tensile deformation at a strain rate of ~10−4 s−1. Test conditions: Torsion tests at 0.05° s−1; tensile tests at ~10−4 s−1; micro-hardness measured with 500 g load for 15 s; microstructure analyzed via SEM, EBSD, and TEM (200 kV). Findings: Yielding strength of the pre-torsioned TWIP steel was doubled to ~730 MPa (from ~300 MPa) with no reduction in ductility.; A gradient nanotwinned structure formed with twin density increasing from the center to the outermost region (r/R=1).; Twin
